Source: https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/26th-october-threat-intelligence-report/
Primary technique report: https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/infostealer-riding-the-ai-train/

The report specifies /gate/handshake, /gate/chunk and /gate/complete. The
handshake atom previously required a quote immediately before /handshake,
missing both prefixed source routes and unquoted native strings. It now
accepts a route suffix with a path/query/fragment/string terminator. Module
filenames and longer words remain excluded. Criticality stays notable.
The existing Aokigahara family composite additionally requires the other two
routes and its gate-token protocol marker. No language, package, endpoint,
attacker filename, token value or build ID is added as a verdict gate.
Only the route atom consumes changed evidence; its exact family consumer and
ancestor references were reviewed. No relocation or new leaf is needed.

Reproduce focused controls (writes only to cleave's external fixtures):
python3 testdata/threat-feed-4355/check.py --fixtures /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/tests/fixtures/threat-feed-4355 --report /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-e78afdd4/scratch/threat-feed/4355/context/controls.json

Ten controls cover Python, JavaScript, native source and a compiled shared
library, prefixed and absolute routes, query strings, filename near misses,
longer route words and generic uploads missing the family marker.

Article samples and provenance are outside the repository:
/usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-e78afdd4/scratch/threat-feed/4355/
Seven original LiteLLM 1.107.0 wheels were recovered using --all-wheels.
The Aokigahara sample is an explicitly labeled JavaScript reconstruction of
cited collection paths and X25519/AES-GCM ZIP-upload protocol, not an original
binary. The hash recovery attempt failed in MalwareBazaar, Triage and Malshare.
No specimen was executed. Facts, extracted code blocks, image/link manifests,
full scans and contextual indicator distinctions are in context/.

Existing LiteLLM coverage includes Chromium password decryption, encrypted
developer/cloud credential export, remote code polling and Python startup
persistence. Broader existing coverage was retained without new duplicates.
The CVE notices do not supply exploit bytes and receive no speculative rules.
Native Aokigahara anti-debugging/configuration routines were not reconstructed;
their behavioral implementation cannot be recovered from the supplied prose.

Final atomscan: all eight hostile samples pass. Each original wheel fires
13 hostile and 9 suspicious traits; the Aokigahara reconstruction fires four
hostile traits (auth catalog, config catalog, their existing conjunction,
and the gated chunk-upload family protocol). No detection-floor retry.
